traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Styracaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely polygamous; ovary superior, half inferior or inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody; flowers in cymes, in racemes or in panicles, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or samara, rarely drupe; stamens (5-) 8 to 10 (-20); carpels (2-) 3 to 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
